summary: Gernot Böhme worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Hamburg from around 1960 to 1965 and held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.
An Indologist, Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1974) under Jan Gonda (~1954–1974). In 1978, he became an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.

Specializing in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Gert Klingenschmitt earned his PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1963–1968). He held posts at Erlangen-Nürnberg (1977, 1981) and chaired Indogermanistik at Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his geshe studies at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Legden. He served at Drepung Gomang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Jampa Tegchok studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993) and as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Gyume Tantric Monastery in 1987 and at Sera Monastery in 1992.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, UBC (2002), and became Director of the LTWA in 2005.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa studied at Gaden Chokor and Sera Monastery under several masters. He served as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 to 1997.
Geshe Lobsang Tharchin worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Gyume Tantric Monastery and at Sera Monastery, where he attained the Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Losang Chödar held positions attested in 2010 at both the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the Institute of Tibetan Classics as a Tibetan editor.

Geshe Lozang Jamspal works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His appointments include the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia University faculty (attested 1985–1990).

Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Geshe Ngawang Nyima studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and Trijang Rinpoche. He held posts at Leiden University (1960) and served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at CIHTS and Ganden Shartse Monastery. He has held visiting posts at Smith, Hampshire, Amherst, and Tasmania, served CIHTS as Director (attested 1990–2019), and taught at Vajrayana Institute.

Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi (attested 1987–1992 and 2004).

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1969–1974) and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Sonam Rinchen studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery (1952–1959), and CIHTS (~1971–1980). Beginning in 1978, he served as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Tashi Tsering studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1987) and Gyuto Monastery, also studying under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery, Gandhi Foundation College, and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (1994).

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye studied at Sera and Gyume Tantric Monasteries under Ling Rinpoche. He taught at both monasteries, was a visiting lecturer at the University of Virginia (1999–2000), and became director at Tibet Center Austria in 2008.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed geshe studies at both Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Yeshe Tobden earned his Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Lodrö Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at CIHTS (~1968–1971).
